prompt.context: You are a consultant for a credit card company that is trying to reduce sizable losses from customers with bad debt. The company uses in-house agents to contact customers who have not paid their bills for 1 to 6 months, with the goal of reaching a settlement where customers pay a percentage of their balance. After 6 months, the accounts are handed off to external collection agents who collect a fee on any money recovered. The in-house agents currently offer customers the option to pay 70% of their balance with no extra finance charges. Requests for less than 70% must be submitted to a supervisor. The supervisor has a 30% floor and typically offers 30%. 30% of all settlements are approved by the supervisor. The total balance of customers targeted for settlements is $600M across 120,000 customers. Currently, 42% of this total balance is recovered through settlements. The company does not yet have data on the percentage of customers by segment that sign up for settlements.
prompt.question: How should the credit card company go about evaluating this process and ultimately recovering the maximum amount from these delinquent customers?

clarifying_info.q: What is the total balance and number of customers targeted?
What percentage is currently being recovered?
clarifying_info.a: 42% of the total balance is currently recovered through settlements.

clarifying_info.q: What settlement terms do in-house agents offer?
clarifying_info.a: Agents offer 70% of balance with no extra finance charges; amounts below 70% go to a supervisor who has a 30% floor and typically offers 30%.

clarifying_info.q: What share of settlements goes to a supervisor?
clarifying_info.a: 30% of all settlements are approved by the supervisor.

clarifying_info.q: Do we have data on how many customers accept settlements by segment?
clarifying_info.a: No, the client does not yet have any data on the percentage of customers by segment that sign up for settlements.

framework: Understand the current state: calculate baseline recovery ($600M x 42% = $252M currently recovered)
Segment delinquent customers: divide by delinquency duration (e.g., 1-3 months past due vs. 3+ months past due) because recovery likelihood differs by how long a customer has been delinquent
Estimate recovery by segment: for each segment, assume number of customers, total balance, % who will accept a settlement, and the settlement terms the company should offer
Compare new segmented approach to current baseline to determine which is more financially desirable
Identify process improvements: introduce intermediate offers before escalating to supervisor; evaluate collection agency terms
Discuss how to arrive at accurate assumptions (data collection, testing)

questions.prompt: Calculate the current amount being recovered under the existing process.
questions.guidance: Simple baseline calculation. Current recovery = total balance x recovery rate.

math.setup: $600M total balance x 42% current recovery rate

questions.prompt: Propose a customer segmentation scheme and explain your rationale.
questions.guidance: A strong answer segments by delinquency duration because the longer a customer has gone without paying, the less likely they are to pay. A reasonable split is 1-3 months past due and 3+ months past due. The candidate should justify assumptions about even spread of customers and balances across segments, and explain that different settlement offers are appropriate for each segment.

questions.prompt: Using your segmentation, estimate the total recovery under the new approach and compare it to the current baseline.
questions.guidance: Candidate should walk through each segment: (1) assume even split of customers and balances, (2) assume a recovery rate (% of customers accepting) and settlement terms for each segment, (3) multiply to get estimated recovery, (4) sum segments and compare to $252M baseline. The example below uses illustrative assumptions; the candidate must state and defend their own.

math.setup: Segment 1 (1-3 months past due): 60K customers, $300M balance, assume 70% accept, offer 50% of balance. Segment 2 (3+ months past due): 60K customers, $300M balance, assume 40% accept, offer 30% of balance.
steps: Compare to baseline: $141M vs. $252M — current method is more financially desirable under these assumptions
math.answer: $141M estimated under example assumptions; current process ($252M) appears superior — but result is highly sensitive to assumptions

questions.prompt: What are the key issues or inefficiencies in the current process, and what improvements would you suggest?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) no customer segmentation — all customers treated the same regardless of delinquency duration; (2) binary negotiation — agents jump straight to supervisor without intermediate offers; suggest intermediate offer steps between 70% and 30% to find the highest acceptable rate without supervisor involvement. Also discuss collection agency terms and whether it is worth pursuing 6+ month accounts internally.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key issues with the current debt recovery process and how can they be addressed?

categories.name: Customer Segmentation
ideas: Segment by months past due (1-3 vs. 3+ months)
Segment by balance size (high-balance vs. low-balance customers)
Segment by payment history or credit score
Tailor settlement offers to each segment's likelihood of paying

categories.name: Negotiation Process Improvements
ideas: Introduce intermediate offers between 70% and 30% before escalating to supervisor
Empower agents to negotiate within a wider band without supervisor approval
Reduce friction in the settlement process to increase acceptance rates
Train agents to identify which customers may accept higher percentages

categories.name: Data & Assumptions
ideas: Collect data on settlement acceptance rates by segment
Run pilots or A/B tests to validate assumptions
Use historical data to build predictive models for recovery likelihood

categories.name: Collection Agency Considerations
ideas: Evaluate the fee structure charged by external collection agents
Assess whether some 6+ month accounts should be kept in-house
Compare net recovery after collection agency fees vs. in-house handling

recommendation: The current process recovers $252M (42% of $600M), which under example assumptions outperforms a simple two-segment approach ($141M); however, the comparison is highly assumption-dependent
Implement customer segmentation by delinquency duration and tailor settlement offers accordingly
Introduce intermediate negotiation steps before escalating to a supervisor to potentially capture higher recovery rates from willing customers
risks: Assumptions about acceptance rates and settlement terms are uncertain — the recommendation could reverse with different inputs
Segmentation approach requires data collection that the client does not currently have
More complex negotiation processes may increase agent workload and cost
next_steps: Collect data on settlement acceptance rates by customer segment
Pilot a segmented offer approach and measure recovery vs. control
Evaluate collection agency contract terms and compare to in-house recovery for 6+ month accounts
Model sensitivity of recovery estimates to key assumption changes
